brief:
Mohammed Salhia, director of the Network of Civil Organizations in Gaza, said humanitarian assistance entering the sector has experienced only limited improvement compared to earlier periods following agreements tied to the second phase of aid operations, the Shehab Wire reported. He noted that despite this modest uptick, delivery levels fall substantially short of Gaza's requirements.

The assessment underscores persistent gaps between aid flowing into the territory and the scale of humanitarian need on the ground. Salhia's comments came as international negotiations aimed at expanding assistance to the blockaded enclave continue, though officials point to recurring shortfalls in meeting basic civilian demands for food, medical supplies, and other essentials.

title: Aid entering Gaza remains inadequate despite modest increase.
